issue.title: Retire remove_vcs_workspace_claims and the TUI meta_workspace reconciliation now that one runner holds one workspace
issue.description:
`remove_vcs_workspace_claims` (`src/sase/ace/tui/models/_dedup.py:209`, called from
`_agent_loader_normalization.py:66`) and the TUI's `meta_workspace` reconciliation
(`models/agent.py`, `_loaders/_workflow_loaders.py`, `_loaders/_workflow_snapshot_loaders.py`,
`thinking/session_resolver.py`, `widgets/prompt_panel/_workflow_render.py`) both exist to
paper over the two-workspace shape epic sase-vd removed: a `#gh:`/`#git:` workflow used to
claim a second workspace the agent record never learned about, so the TUI had to drop the
synthetic VCS claim rows and prefer `step_output.meta_workspace` over `agent.workspace_num`.

After sase-vd, a runner holds exactly one numbered claim, and its RUNNING row, `done.json`,
occupant record, and shell member meta all name it. The reconciliation should now be dead
weight on live agents.

FOUND BY: the epic sase-vd plan explicitly deferred this
(`plan:202608/one_workspace_per_agent_family.md`, "Out of scope": "retiring them is
follow-up work, and a task should be filed for it rather than folded in here"). The
sase-vd land agent filed it after confirming both call sites are still live on master.

Worth its own investigation rather than a straight deletion: historical agent artifacts on
disk still carry `step_output.meta_workspace` and pre-sase-vd double-claim rows, so the
work has to decide what the loaders do for records written before this epic, not just
delete the branches.

task_type_fields.proposal: Remove `remove_vcs_workspace_claims` and the `step_output.meta_workspace` preference from the ACE agent loaders, so the TUI reads one workspace identity per agent straight from the agent record, and decide explicitly how pre-sase-vd artifacts on disk are handled.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic sase-vd (One workspace per agent family) named this in its Out of scope section: phases 1-3 make the reconciliation dead weight, but retiring it is a separate change with its own backward-compatibility question about historical agent records.

payload.close_reason: Superseded by active epic sase-x7's canonical-contracts/remove-layout-migrations work (sase-x7.9 and sase-x7.11). remove_vcs_workspace_claims and meta_workspace reconciliation are explicitly old two-workspace compatibility behavior; the epic owns canonicalizing reachable metadata before deleting such readers, while preserving historical information. Transferred these exact symbols and the historical-record caveat to sase-x7. A parallel deletion worker would race the epic's migration certificates and could remove a reader before its inputs are converted. This closes duplicate ownership, not the still-present code.
